items.title: Think of an everyday item — we've tracked how much the price has gone up
items.description: If it feels like everything is getting more expensive, that's because it is. With the rate of inflation rising this week, we've tracked how the price of everyday items has increased.

items.title: Israel’s massive strike was opposite of surgical, Lebanon deputy PM says
items.description: Lebanon's deputy prime minister Tarek Mitri says the government cannot exercise its authority over the country while Israel continues its bombardments and occupation.

items.title: Hanson billed taxpayers for flights to fundraiser, to catch Florida jet
items.description: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson billed taxpayers for two trips that included party fundraisers, discussions with disaffected National Barnaby Joyce, a Gina Rinehart event and return flights to connect the senator to her private jet to Florida, sponsored by her major donor, Mrs Rinehart.

items.title: I don't want cold pasta for dinner: Why my appliances aren't cutting it
items.description: While the newest home technology aims to make life easier, when it prioritises aesthetics over usability, some lives are actually made much harder, writes Nas Campanella.

items.title: Coalition's risky Farrer strategy could clear path for One Nation
items.description: Pauline Hanson is now set to tour more regional Coalition-held seats in her "sexy" new private plane, and the Liberal and National parties are helping clear the runway.

items.title: Has the world’s most powerful cartel met its end?
items.description: A United Arab Emirates decision to pull the plug on its OPEC membership could be the nail in the coffin for an organisation that has struggled to keep its members in line for 66 years.

items.title: ‘It’s a safety issue’: Construction industry faces gambling crisis
items.description: New research reveals 89 per cent of construction workers have gambled in the past year — higher than the national average.

items.title: 'Only a little baby': Family of missing 5yo Sharon Granites speaks
items.description: Family members of a missing Alice Springs five-year-old have spoken to the ABC for the first time, pleading for anyone with information that could help find their "energetic" little girl to come forward.

items.title: Insurers among group proposing cheaper premiums for disaster-resistant homes
items.description: As about 1.6 million households experience insurance unaffordability stress, a disparate alliance of stakeholders proposes cheaper premiums for home owners who upgrade their properties to withstand natural disasters.

items.title: UK police declare terrorist incident after two Jewish men stabbed in London
items.description: A man has been arrested after two men were stabbed in London in an area with a large Jewish population.

items.title: 'Extremely corrosive': Trump called out for remarks aimed at Australia
items.description: US congressman Joe Courtney says the US president's repeated criticism of Australia is "unfair" and causing harm to the US amongst its allies.

items.title: King visits 9/11 memorial as he tours New York
items.description: King Charles III and Queen Camilla met survivors and family members of victims, as well as with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

items.title: 'Accident' helps identify giant 'shark-toothed' dinosaur's skull fragment
items.description: Two fossils found in Thailand are named as long-missing pieces of a "shark-toothed" dinosaur after being identified partly by accident.

items.title: APRA Music Awards winners for 2026 announced
items.description: Punk rockers Amyl and The Sniffers have bagged three top gongs at the Australian music industry's APRA awards.

items.title: Gifted, goofy, gone too soon: Jeff Buckley's genius remembered
items.description: The otherworldly singer-guitarist died at 30 and struggled with fame. His guitarist and a new movie honour Buckley's humanity and musical genius.

items.title: Navigating bull dust and racing the sun on the Binns Track
items.description: Journeying through the Binns Track in remote central Australia, Rae Johnston learns why you should always travel with mates.

items.title: Flag quiz: Line up for our fiendishly hard flag quiz!
items.description: Do you know the Union Jack from the Stars and Stripes? And which flags aren't rectangular?

items.title: 'No offence to Tassie': The infamous Sirengate mess 20 years on
items.description: Two decades ago, two teams met at York Park in Launceston. The siren sounded but the match continued and the dreaded word "gate" was added to another footy scandal.

items.title: First report from antisemitism, Bondi royal commission to be released
items.description: The Royal Commission into Antisemitism and Social Cohesion will deliver its first report, two months after it began and less than six months after the Bondi Beach terror attack.

items.title: What we know about the fatal plane crash in Adelaide
items.description: Investigations are underway into a light plane crash at an airport in Adelaide's north that claimed two lives and injured 10 others.

items.title: 'Free Palestine' party plans to funnel votes to Victorian conservatives
items.description: Victorian voters are being urged to look out for "misleading" party names, as right-wing activists seek to redirect progressive votes to conservative parties.

items.title: Interpreter shortage leaving non-English speakers at risk in court
items.description: As Brisbane courts face delays and backlogs, cases involving people with limited English are being adjourned when interpreters are unavailable — a problem advocates warn is set to worsen.

items.title: 'Big lif' is spelling big problems for Vanuatu's pristine rainforests
items.description: A habitat-destroying invasive species is taking over Vanuatu's forests, but one village is fighting back and earning an income for its people at the same time.

items.title: Inside this council's failed campaign to sell the four-day work week
items.description: It wanted to be the first Australian council to usher in a four-day work week. Documents show there was never a standalone business case to back the proposal — but there was a tight grip on messaging.

items.title: Inflation details may give RBA pause for thought on interest rates
items.description: While inflation remains well above the Reserve Bank's target, there are details in the numbers that may give it reasons to hold off another rate hike in May.
